questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to try to live surrounded by grand nature so i thought iceland could be very exotic in a nordic noir kind off way:) the active volcano, the northern lights, the night life, puffins and whales - everything turned out to be just how i wished for it to be. 10/10

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: more or less, i mean there is alotalot of administrative work when it comes to planning an exchange. But i managed to find a information desk on campus where i was pointed to the international office. they helped me with everything. But i had a lot of questions regarding courses, since one of the courses i got pre-approved suddenly wasn't being taught in the autumn semester. but they helped me with everything and i got the credits transferred that i needed being a ERASMUS student.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was pointed to the international office at UGLA.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found some facebook pages for internationals looking for short-term accommodation. I made a post and a cute lady reached out to me and we planned for me to rent her apartment for 5 months. A really nice place on the main shopping street in Reykjavik f(Laugavegur<33) for approx 5000 DKK

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: funfunfun but bare in mind that the student accommodation on campus is 2-3km from downtown reykjavik, which can be annoying when going out. There is no metro or equivalent to s-trains, so you have to walk or rent a scooter, which can be brutal in icelandic winter. ((i know that 2-3km doesn't sound like a lot, but Reykjavik is a tiny tiny village so your sense of distance will be changed radically:))

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: its difficult as a bachelor student to find courses that matches your mandatory courses, so i spend a lot of time making that work. The process was very stressfull, but it can be done:)

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: easy - the canvas student intranet is the exact same as abalone, so i just added the courses i got pre-approved from KU

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: the international office and the information desk on campus

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 10/10 i got everything transferred

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: take all courses on small states  !! - the professors are AMAZING. I had two courses on small states (that covered DAK and EP) and honestly i have never felt so academically inspired, which is something i veryvery rarely feel :´)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: the professors are amazing, the classes very small and intimate. You get participation grades which at first is very intimidating, but i learned to love it. You really get to debate everything which forces you to read the course material and analyze upon it.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: i did a lot of master level classes as a BA student and i did well. It was my experience that KU has a higher level for politcal science than most other countries.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The classes were typically only 11 students, so a lot of debating and conversation with the professor. No large lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
small states in eu
small states in IR
gender studies
crisis management

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: small states both in eu and IR. or just anything with Baldur Thorhallson

questions.answer: i didn't take use of any of the activities i was busy going to cafes with my cute new friends :)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
AMAZING cute good cafes with a proper flat white: reykjavik roasters, Nikki refurbs and kaffivest 
nature : rent a camper van, clear 5-7 days, gather some friends and drive the ring road around iceland.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy as a fellow scandi

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: just be youuuu<3

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
island people! insular in some ways.. but amazingly sweet,
warm.and
progressive. Be aware of the post-colonial history between danes and icelanders. there is a animosity towards danes especially amongst the elderly icelanders

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: very feminist state, super woke and inclusive of minorities

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) flat white at reykjavik roaster and orange wine at mikki refur
2) take the courses which is taught by Baldur Thorhallson (he is a superstar on campus, ole wæver vibe)
3) rent a campervan and travel around the entire of Iceland (follow the ring road, ITS INSANELY beautiful)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: i now have friends for life all over the world<33 I visit them, they visit me and it is SO REWARDING.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: nothing was challenging during the exchange, but the administrative work leading up to my exchange was so confusing and challenging
